mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Earth is the same as its neighbouring term in this chapter, so the decision does not change.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: Too-hot or too-cold conditions do not satisfy the liquid-water condition for life as described in the chapter.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: temperature range -> liquid water can exist -> habitability becomes possible happens first, and that produces orbital distance.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when Too-hot or too-cold conditions do not satisfy the liquid-water condition for life as described in the chapter is not true.

intelligence.enrichment: Earth is at the right distance from the Sun, where the temperature is neither too hot nor too cold, allowing water to exist in liquid form in the habitable zone. orbital distance -> temperature range -> liquid water can exist -> habitability becomes possible The learner correctly uses the chapter relationship: Earth is at the right distance from the Sun, where the temperature is neither too hot nor too cold, allowing water to exist in liquid form in the habitable zone. A planet is habitable whenever it has the label Blue Planet or is near Earth in space.
